solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chart turned out in capital of Mozambique

parts.note: a chart is a map

indicators.note: turned signals that the little word beside it, out, is shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A map was produced in the Mozambican capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Maputo is the capital city of Mozambique, on the Indian Ocean coast.

clue.text: Ma involved with I Ching in US state

indicators.note: involved, in the sense of tangled up, tells us the letters of Ma and I Ching are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mother takes up the Chinese divination book somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Michigan is one of the fifty states, in the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Hand out round sticker to top French department

indicators.note: round says the distributing word is wrapped around the sticker and the top-quality pieces

parts.note: to hand out is to pass
a decal is a sticker
A1 (written AI) means top-quality, first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone distributes a round sticker to the leading French administrative area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand out' reads as a verb phrase but just gives a synonym; A1 is the old Lloyd's Register mark for first-class, written here as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas-de-Calais is a French administrative department on the Channel coast.

clue.text: Empty tarpaulin in burgh in Easter Ross

indicators.note: emptying the word tarpaulin means scooping out its middle, leaving the two letters at each end

explanation.surface: An empty tarp lies in a small Highland town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' takes RPAUL from the middle of TARPAULIN, leaving its ends. A burgh is a Scottish town with a charter, and Easter Ross is an area in the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tain is a small royal burgh in Easter Ross, in the Scottish Highlands, known for its whisky distillery.

clue.text: 6's wrong note removed in German state capital

indicators.note: wrong says what remains is put into the wrong order, an anagram
removed says the note's letters are taken away from the cross-referenced word

parts.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down, the cathedral city
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A city's mistaken musical note was cut out in a German state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 down gives WINCHESTER; 'removed' takes TE out of it to leave WINCHESR, and 'wrong' anagrams those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwerin is the capital of the German state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

clue.text: Class looted wildly in Spanish holiday area

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of class looted run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A gang of thieves rampages through a resort coast in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa del Sol is the sunny southern coast of Spain, popular with package holidaymakers.

clue.text: Rifle hard disk in cathedral city

explanation.surface: Someone ransacks a hard drive in an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions. 'Rifle' looks like a verb (to ransack) but is the gun; Winchester city in Hampshire has a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester repeating rifle is a famous gun, early hard drives were nicknamed Winchester disks, and Winchester is a Hampshire cathedral city.

clue.text: Traitor regularly holding port

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of traitor, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A turncoat is keeping hold of a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro, often just Rio, is a major Brazilian seaport.

clue.text: Partners accepting stake in French port

indicators.note: accepting means the partners take the stake in between them

parts.note: North and South are partners in bridge
an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: Two partners take a wager in a French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North and South play as partners, giving N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a French city and port on the River Loire.

clue.text: From French and German county

parts.note: de is French for from
von is the German for from, as in noble names

explanation.surface: Someone hails from a place in France and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' does duty in both languages: DE in French, VON in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon is a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Fortress protecting island on former Spanish kingdom

indicators.note: protecting means the fortress surrounds the island letter

parts.note: a castle is a fortress

explanation.surface: A fort guards an island in an old Spanish realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile was a medieval kingdom of central Spain that united with Aragon.

clue.text: Joiner scattered around Isle of Wight resort

indicators.note: around says the scattered word goes round the joiner

parts.note: sown, as seed is, means scattered
and is a joining word, a conjunction

explanation.surface: A carpenter scattered about an English island seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandown is a seaside town on the east coast of the Isle of Wight, off southern England.

clue.text: Tip off banker in Buckinghamshire town

indicators.note: tip off means the first letter, the tip, is cut away

parts.note: in crosswords a banker is a river, something with banks

explanation.surface: A warning is given to a bank employee in a home-counties town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip off' pretends to mean a warning and 'banker' a financier; Buckinghamshire is a county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Iver is a village town in south Buckinghamshire, near Pinewood film studios.

clue.text: Duke having gone ahead, wandering to Ulster resort

indicators.note: wandering says the letters of gone ahead stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman has set off ahead, roaming towards a Northern Irish seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Donaghadee is a seaside town in County Down, Northern Ireland, which is often called Ulster.

clue.text: Dusky fleck's first seen on lecturer in white coat in burgh in Fife

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown, dusky colour

indicators.note: the fleck's first means just the initial letter of fleck is used
in says the lecturer letter sits within the white coat

parts.note: ermine is the white winter coat of the stoat

explanation.surface: A dark speck shows up on an academic in a white coat in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a region of eastern Scotland; a burgh is a chartered Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunfermline is a historic town in Fife, once Scotland's royal capital.

clue.text: Make slender rods in river on Greek islands

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing

indicators.note: in says the rods go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and also Scotland
canes are slender rods

explanation.surface: Someone fashions thin sticks in a river on a Greek island group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dodecanese is a group of Greek islands in the south-east Aegean, including Rhodes.

clue.text: Joplin composition playing in Spanish region

parts.note: Scott Joplin composed ragtime pieces, so one of his works is a rag
a record that is playing is on

explanation.surface: A Scott Joplin piece is being played somewhere in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragon is an autonomous region of north-east Spain, once a kingdom.

clue.text: Forces' canteen at a Sicilian seaport

parts.note: a mess is where military personnel eat
at a place is in it

explanation.surface: An army mess hall is located in a Sicilian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in north-east Sicily, facing the Italian mainland across its strait.

clue.text: F1 champion will laugh with author in Canada

parts.note: ha is a laugh
John Milton was the author of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A Formula One champion will share a laugh with a writer in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue packs in a third definition too: Hamilton is a city in Ontario, Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Hamilton is a multiple Formula One world champion.

clue.text: Coffer in aircraft in London street

indicators.note: in says the coffer is put inside the aircraft

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A strongbox is stowed aboard a plane in a London street.
explanation.definitionFit: Park Lane is a grand street in Mayfair, London, alongside Hyde Park.

clue.text: Food for the table with cooked meat in Hampshire town

parts.note: fare is food served at table
ham is cured and cooked pork

explanation.surface: Dinner is served with cold cuts in a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fareham is a market town in Hampshire, between Southampton and Portsmouth.

clue.text: Amateur clergyman, say, returning to Swiss city

indicators.note: returning says the whole string of pieces is read back to front

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A lay preacher, perhaps, goes back to a city in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a major city in Switzerland on Lake Geneva.

clue.text: Take in this hack finally in Yorkshire racecourse town

indicators.note: in says the take letter goes inside the word this

parts.note: R, from Latin recipe, means take on prescriptions

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of hack

explanation.surface: Accept this journalist at last in a northern racing town.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsk is a market town in North Yorkshire with a well-known horse-racing course.

clue.text: Trivial criticism upset missing German in Scottish burgh

indicators.note: missing means the German letter is left out
upset in a down clue turns the word over, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: a niggle is a petty criticism

explanation.surface: Petty complaint, upset at the loss of a German, in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses NIGGLE to ELGGIN, and 'missing' removes one G.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a historic town in Moray, Scotland, famous for its ruined cathedral.

clue.text: OAPs in hail storm on West Indian island

indicators.note: storm signals the letters of OAPs in hail are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Pensioners caught in a hailstorm on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: OAPs are old-age pensioners in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispaniola is the Caribbean island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Smoke billowing out east in Siberia

indicators.note: billowing says the remaining letters swirl into a new order
out means the east letter is thrown out of the word smoke

explanation.surface: Smoke billows out eastward over Siberia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from SMOKE, and 'billowing' anagrams SMOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in south-western Siberia, Russia, so a place found there.

clue.text: Left out of the sun on Leicester's river

indicators.note: out of means the left letter is dropped from the sun word

parts.note: solar means of the sun

explanation.surface: Someone is left out of the sunshine by a Midlands river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soar is a river flowing through Leicester in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Pre-Raphaelite short of town near Wrexham

indicators.note: short of means the last letter is clipped off

parts.note: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was a Pre-Raphaelite painter and poet

explanation.surface: A Victorian painter falls short of reaching a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrexham is a town in north-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossett is a village town just north of Wrexham, in Wales.

clue.text: See 5
One nameless female taking in Japanese institute on Pacific island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: taking in says the shortened female surrounds the next two letters
nameless means the abbreviation for name, N, is dropped

parts.note: a woman is a female

explanation.surface: A single anonymous woman takes in a Japanese institution on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' cuts N from WOMAN to leave WOMA, which takes in J and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima is a small Pacific island, scene of a famous 1945 battle.

clue.text: Where Irish cats fight and reportedly murder young lad

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: to kill is to murder; Kenny is a boy's name, a pet form of Kenneth, so a young lad

explanation.surface: A grim scene of feline fights and the killing of a boy in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kilkenny cats' are a byword for fighting till nothing is left of either, from an Irish legend about two cats that fought until only their tails remained.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend of the Kilkenny cats places two cats fighting to the death in that Irish city.

clue.text: Musical heard in the country

indicators.note: heard says what follows is how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: Grease is a stage and screen musical

explanation.surface: A musical is performed out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' reads as rural land, but names one particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe.
